provenance.selection: Completed JSON objects with label and samples fields, including failed commands, discovered recursively beneath the local experiment directory. Cargo metadata and GitHub release API dumps are excluded.
provenance.log_location: Each sample names a log basename retained only in the ignored local experiment directory.
provenance.privacy: Absolute repository/home paths are replaced with aliases. Unrelated project names and all process IDs are removed; boundary counts, process kinds, and presence flags are retained.

hardware.storage: Samsung PM981-family NVMe; repository and relocated MBX cache share an XFS filesystem with reflink enabled

toolchains.gpu_build_acceleration: No GPU compiler/linker acceleration was measured or enabled.

method.wall_clock: Python time.perf_counter around the complete command, including process startup, waits, compilation, linking, and tests when requested.
method.resource_measurement: /usr/bin/time reports user_seconds, system_seconds, and max_rss_kib for the timed command and measured descendants. CPU and RSS do not include work in retained/background daemons. Maximum RSS is not aggregate system memory.
method.sampling: Normally one warmup followed by three measured iterations. Some population/restore probes contain one sample. Warmups and failed samples remain in reports but are excluded from successful summary medians.

desktop-edit.change: Insert a unique run/iteration suffix into the error-format string.

core-edit.change: Append a unique run/iteration suffix to the context string.

source_edits.restoration: The harness restores the original source bytes on completion and records the original source SHA-256. It stops rather than overwriting an external source change.
source_edits.warmup_edit: When true, the warmup itself changes source to seed the first incremental source edit. Otherwise warmup uses original source. Earlier reports omit this field; their recorded samples are preserved.

method.environment: Each report retains the recorded allowlisted environment overrides, not a complete shell environment. Wrapper defaults and profile contents evolved during the session; preserve label/config distinctions when comparing results.
method.contention: Process snapshots occur only before and after samples. A presence flag means a matching compiler/build process was observed; it does not measure its CPU utilization or prove continuous contention. Retained idle daemons can appear. Older snapshots lack process kind and are labeled unspecified-build-process. Reports before verify-check-unchanged excluded processes whose cwd matched the measured checkout. The final harness also records those processes. Known overlapping same-project work is called out explicitly where relevant.
caveats: Experiments were sequential opportunistic probes on a machine with varying unrelated build activity, not randomized isolated trials. Boundary snapshots cannot account for all load or thermal variation.
Source edits change strings and represent one small application or core change; other edits, feature sets, and dependency updates can have different costs.

No end-to-end clean plain-Cargo baseline paired with MBX population/restore was measured. The 123.7971 s population and 26.8972 s restore are different cache states and had varying contention; they do not establish a clean-Cargo speedup ratio.

The 36.8977 s integrated MBX/Wild fresh-target restore uses eager incremental mode and a final-binary Wild adapter, differing from the 26.8972 s non-eager restore. It is not a fair fresh-cache winner comparison.
Codec fixture and core-loop commands include execution of the selected test. Faster optimized fixtures do not imply an equal improvement in compiler-only time.
Blaze runs used a different nightly/compiler architecture, retained daemon state, and did not complete a successful check. Their low client CPU/RSS must not be interpreted as low total work.
The first Wild invocation failed to select the linker. Only linker-wild-fixed supplies a successful adapter measurement.
Three successful samples give a small local observation, not a statistically established universal speedup. Warmups include profile/cache preparation costs and are retained for transparency.

combined_fixture_runs.scope: Repeated unchanged fixture-test command; includes test runtime, not a source-edit build.
Repeated unchanged fixture-test command; includes test runtime, not a source-edit build.

selected_comparisons.name: Fixed Wild adapter versus default LLD
selected_comparisons.scope: Small desktop source edit, final crate compile and link under dev-fast
selected_comparisons.caveat: Separate short trials; preserve contention and warmup context. This is command wall time, not isolated linker time.

selected_comparisons.name: Optimized core test loop versus dev-fast
selected_comparisons.scope: Core source edit followed by the exact codec fixture test
selected_comparisons.caveat: Includes compilation and fixture execution; profile.dev-test.package.shadowroom.opt-level=2. Both have source-edit warmups; varying contention remains.

integrated_restore_details.note: Cache/compile details supplied by the completed local run log; these timings can overlap and are not additive command wall time.
